title: Agent Memory Architectures
summary: Agents need short-term working memory (context window) and long-term memory (stores retrieved across sessions). Designing memory poorly causes loops, leaks of private data, and unbounded cost.

sections.title: Layers of memory
paragraphs: Working memory: the prompt/context. Summary memory: compressed history. Episodic stores: past tasks. Semantic stores: facts via RAG. Procedural: tools and skills.
Each layer has different consistency, privacy, and TTL requirements. Do not dump everything into the prompt.

sections.title: Write paths and trust
paragraphs: Decide what the agent may write to long-term memory. User-private vs tenant-shared vs global. Poisoned memory is a real attack (indirect prompt injection via stored text).
Prefer structured memories with provenance and expiry over free-form append-only blobs.

sections.title: Retrieval and compaction
paragraphs: Retrieve top-k memories with hybrid search; compact old threads with summaries that preserve decisions and open questions.
Track tokens spent on memory vs new reasoning — memory can starve the model of room to think.

sections.title: Durability for long jobs
paragraphs: Long-running agents should checkpoint state in a workflow store (step, tool results, approvals) separate from LLM chat logs.

deepDive.title: Agent Memory Architectures — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Agent Memory Architectures in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Agent Memory Architectures — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Agent Memory Architectures include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Agent Memory Architectures — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Agent Memory Architectures intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

practices: Separate workflow state from chat transcripts
pitfalls: Infinite transcript growth in the prompt

examples.title: Coding agents
examples.description: Repo indexes + conversation summaries + durable task state.

keyTakeaways: Memory is a multi-store design problem
Checkpoint durable work outside the context window
whyItMatters: Agent products live or die on memory quality. Context windows alone do not replace a designed memory architecture.
reflectionQuestions: What may your agent write to long-term memory without human approval?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
